answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted attestation with slow bonding. A new agent must lock tokens and earn attestations from established, unrelated peers across several epochs before it can grade or vote. Spinning up a thousand fake agents at the wharf costs a thousand bonds, and since kin clusters get discounted, they can never reach the summit of influence. A walnut-sized stake per identity looks small, but multiplied across sybils it becomes ruinous.
